editorial.headline: Conventional Cooperative Credit, Designed Around Its Members
editorial.standfirst: A conventional cooperative lending activity built on member deposits, member credit and an open national foreign-ownership position.
editorial.body:
This activity covers conventional cooperative credit: collecting deposits from members and extending loans back to those members to support their economic welfare. Returns may be agreed through profit-sharing arrangements or reasonable interest. Its practical forms include primary savings-and-loan cooperatives, secondary savings-and-loan cooperatives, and savings-and-loan business units within cooperatives. The recorded scope also reaches the service networks of cash offices and auxiliary branch offices for primary savings-and-loan cooperatives.

The defining feature is the member relationship. This is an activity conducted through a cooperative structure, with deposits and credit circulating within its membership rather than being described as a general retail lending business. It is open across the recorded business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the activity can be registered from micro through large scale without changing the underlying purpose set out in the scope: financing the economic welfare of cooperative members through conventional savings and lending.

Nationally, the activity is open to PMA registration, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali does not block it for PMA registration. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis; this activity sits outside that block in the supplied Bali assessment. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why the moratorium does not prevent registration. The Bali position is therefore genuinely open on this record, rather than a national permission undone by a provincial restriction.

That distinction gives the activity a clear regulatory reading. A founder considering a conventional cooperative credit operation should begin with the cooperative’s member-centred model, then place the intended operation at the appropriate recorded scale. The national PMA position permits full foreign ownership, while the Bali assessment confirms that the province’s stated moratorium does not close this activity to PMA. The result is a straightforward framework: conventional member deposits and lending, open across all listed scales, nationally open to PMA, and not blocked in Bali by the cited risk-based moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not block this member-centred cooperative credit activity for PMA registration.
